basic_identification.sector_category: Water Resources / Hydraulic Gates and Valves (approved by the Water Resources Division Council and finalized by the Hydraulic Gates and Valves Sectional Committee, WRD 12, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Hydraulic Gates and Valves Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies guidelines, operational parameters, and structural design criteria for de-icing systems (particularly compressed air bubbler systems) installed on hydraulic structures—such as spillway gates, radial gates, fixed-wheel gates, and trash-rack structures—in cold and sub-freezing regions to prevent ice formation and ensure trouble-free gate operation.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Code of Practice / Design and Operational Guidelines (Water Resources Department)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 10021:2000 is an engineering guideline and operational code of practice for dam outfitting and hydraulic gates rather than a direct consumer product, it does not carry a mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp. However, compliance with its technical specifications, air-bubble layout schematics, and pressure curve requirements is strictly mandated in public sector hydropower development tenders (under NHPC, SJVN, NEEPCO, etc.) and dam design audits across sub-freezing regions of India (such as Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Sikkim) to ensure structural safety and prevent freezing disasters.

requirements.detail: Requires preparing an operational calibration curve showing compressor discharge pressures for varying reservoir water levels, based on the specific operating characteristics of the compressor, to match changing hydrostatic heads as the reservoir level rises and falls.
The proper use of control valves for both the operating cycle and the shutdown cycle of the de-icing system must be explicitly described in the operating instructions.

Submerged compressed air nozzles are positioned at standard intervals, typically spaced at 3-metre center-to-center distances (3 m ± tolerance) to establish a continuous rising bubble curtain of warm water.
De-icing distribution piping must be securely integrated with trash racks and spillway gate structures to prevent interference with hoisting machinery or rubbish cleaning operations.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 10021 : 2000 is the national Indian Standard guidelines specifying de-icing systems for hydraulic installations such as spillways, gates, and trash racks in sub-freezing climates. It outlines the design and operation of compressed air bubbler systems, which release bubbles through submerged piping to circulate warmer bottom water to the surface, melting ice and ensuring gate operability. It mandates calibrating compressor discharge pressures against varying reservoir water levels and requires clear operational instructions for control valves during running and shutdown cycles.
